波.meaning: A bear spreads an old fur <part>pelt</part> on the sea like a rug and lies down on it. The <part>water drops</part> lift and roll it, up and down, until the bear is bobbing far from shore. It's riding the <kanji>waves</kanji>.
波.on: It washes up next to a little beach <sound>hu</sound>t.
波.kun: It shares a warm <sound>na</sound>an with the <sound>mee</sound>rkat who runs the hut.

津.meaning: After a storm, a battered little boat spots a painter on the shore. With one huge <part>brush</part> she sweeps a calm curve into the <part>water drops</part>, and the waves inside it go flat. The boat glides in and rests at last. It has found a <kanji>haven</kanji>.
津.on: The sailor jumps ashore and bangs his <sound>shin</sound> on the dock.
津.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' he sneezes, dripping wet, and the painter wraps him in a towel.

処.meaning: An office clerk finds a pile of junk in the hall: a broken <part>folding chair</part> and a wobbly <part>table</part>. She folds the chair flat, flips the table, and carries both out to the skip in one trip. Problem handled: she knows how to <kanji>dispose</kanji> of things.
処.on: Then she sells the screws to a junk <sound>sho</sound>p round the corner.
処.kun: Now there's room for a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, which a <sound>ko</sound>ala carves while a <sound>ro</sound>dent watches: a nice place.

箋.meaning: A knight snaps his <part>spear</part> into a dozen neat pens and opens a little shop. On the shelves: thin <part>bamboo</part> paper, envelopes, labels and wax seals, stacked in tidy piles. He sells <kanji>stationery</kanji>.
箋.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try off duty buys a sheet to write home.
箋.kun: The knight sticks a label on a rolled-up <sound>fu</sound>ton and sings 'Ta-<sound>da</sound>!'

混.meaning: At a family party, all the <part>descendants</part>, from grandkids to great-great-grandkids, pour their own <part>water drops</part> into one big punch bowl: lemonade, tea, milk, juice. Grandma stirs it all together. It's quite a <kanji>mix</kanji>.
混.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor swoops down and gives it one more stir with its wing.
混.kun: Then a lla<sound>ma</sound> dips its head in and mixes in some hay.

雑.meaning: Halfway up a <part>tree</part>, <part>nine</part> <part>sparrow</part> stallholders run a junk sale, one per branch: a single sock, a cracked teacup, a kazoo, half a map, a spoon with a bite out of it. Nothing matches anything else. The sign nailed to the trunk just says <kanji>miscellaneous</kanji>.
雑.on: It's the oddest stall in the whole ba<sound>za</sound>ar, and the dust off the junk makes the smallest sparrow sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
雑.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>!' cheeps a chick, digging a toy <sound>jee</sound>p out from under the socks: everything here is all mixed in together.

帯.meaning: A tightrope walker's costume is a mess: a <part>comb</part> stuck in her hair, a <part>blanket</part> round her shoulders, a <part>towel</part> round her hips. Before she steps onto the rope, her coach ties the whole lot in place with one long silk <kanji>sash</kanji>.
帯.on: Out of silk for the second knot, the coach whips off his own <sound>tie</sound> and wraps it round her waist as well.
帯.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' she gasps, halfway across, as the sash slips up to her neck, and she wears it as a scarf to the end.

携.meaning: A tiny sailor <part>sparrow</part> packs for a voyage: a pocket-sized <part>anchor</part>, and a <part>folding ruler</part> that snaps down small enough to tuck under one wing. Everything she owns folds up and flies with her. Her whole life is <kanji>portable</kanji>.
携.on: Under the other wing she carries a little birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke, folded neatly in half.
携.kun: '<sound>Ta</sound>-da!' she chirps, landing, and unpacks a picnic she brought all the way: a yu<sound>zu</sound> and a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines.
